subject: Cutover flakiness — fragmented SYN-ACKs + SNAT drift on private link
messages:
From: Mike Chang <mike.chang@brightline.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai; vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: ClearHarbor NetOps <netops@clearharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Persistent packet truncation after scheduled cutover

Hey Redwood team,

We rolled the private link cutover at 03:00 UTC this morning and started seeing intermittent connection failures to our on-prem services. Symptoms:
- Multiple client sessions see immediate RST or TCP stream truncation shortly after the 3-way handshake completes (SYN->SYN/ACK->ACK).
- Packet captures show SYN/ACKs arriving but with an unexpected smaller payload and often with the DF bit set; retransmits sometimes succeed.
- Failures correlate with heavy outbound bursts from our environment.

Attached is a short tcpdump + tcpflow slice (diagnostic-trace-20260908.txt) and the ticket we opened with ClearHarbor (CH-3847). Can you confirm whether any SNAT or MTU/ MSS policy changed during the cutover? This started immediately after your announced maintenance.

We need this triaged urgently — several internal services are reporting failed syncs.

Thanks,
Mike Chang
Network Engineering
Brightline Systems

Mike — thanks for the traces and the heads up. I'm looking now. Quick questions while I dig in:
- Can you confirm the MTU on your on-prem edge (physical interface) and whether any MSS-clamp is set on the ClearHarbor firewall?
- Which VIP/ routed prefix are the failing sessions using? If you can paste the 5-tuple for a failed session that would help.

Initial hunch: truncated SYN/ACKs + DF set often point to PMTU/fragmentation issues or an intermediate device doing aggressive MSS clamping. Also will validate whether our SNAT pool changed in the cutover (our cutover included a temporary migration of SNAT service to a new NAT gateway).

I'll pull internal traces and get back with a remediation plan.

—Vanessa
Principal Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Mike Chang <mike.chang@brightline.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent packet truncation after scheduled cutover

Hi all — analyzed the tcpdump slice. TL;DR: two contributing issues — SNAT ephemeral-port aliasing during the migration plus the ClearHarbor egress firewall is not applying MSS-clamp for the path, so large MSS values are resulting in intermediate devices dropping/fragmenting SYN/ACKs with DF set.

Key findings (excerpt from trace):
- 10.1.5.12:49823 -> 198.51.100.22:443: SYN, seq=0
- 198.51.100.22:443 -> 10.1.5.12:49823: SYN/ACK, payload len=40, MSS option=1460, DF=1
- Client sends ACK -> immediate RST seen within ~120ms on ~20% samples

Observations:
- During the cutover our SNAT service switched to a new gateway (gw-snat-07) and the translation table shows reuse of ephemeral ports across different flows in a short window (we see collisions in the mapping table). That can cause surprising state resets on some NAT implementations when the backend stack ties flow id to ephemeral port + sequence ranges.
- The ClearHarbor firewall drops fragments when DF=1 and there is MTU mismatch; they are not applying MSS clamp on TCP SYNs from our side (their default security posture).

Recommended mitigations (short window):
1) Apply a temporary 1:1 SNAT mapping for the failing prefix (198.51.100.0/28) so ephemeral port aliasing cannot occur while we stabilize the migration. This requires an ACL change on gw-snat-07 (low risk, immediate).
2) Ask ClearHarbor to enable MSS-clamp to 1380 on the egress firewall for Brightline -> Redwood paths (we have a documented path where a 1400+ MSS triggers fragments).
3) If MSS-clamp cannot be enabled quickly, schedule a small maintenance to reduce MSS on the client-side (as a last resort) or add explicit MTU discovery logs.

Attachments: topology-v2.png (shows current cutover SNAT topology and where gw-snat-07 sits). I've also attached a short excerpt of the NAT table and collision counts.

I'll prepare the exact ACL snippet to pin the prefix to a 1:1 mapping; need Stephanie or a gatekeeper to approve a one-hour window to apply and monitor.

—Karthik
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Cutover flakiness — fragmented SYN-ACKs + SNAT drift on private link

Laura — escalating so we can get sign-off for the temporary 1:1 SNAT change and for a joint MSS-clamp request to ClearHarbor. Summary + next steps below:

Summary:
- Issue: Intermittent connection truncation after cutover. Root causes: transient SNAT ephemeral-port aliasing on our new gw-snat-07 plus ClearHarbor not applying MSS-clamp -> packet fragments dropped (DF=1).
- Impact: ~15-25% of client sessions for a small set of prefixes fail under bursty traffic; Brightline customer impact: sync failures and degraded service.

Proposed immediate actions (seeking approval):
- Apply 1:1 SNAT for 198.51.100.0/28 on gw-snat-07 for a 1-hour window (apply at 00:30 UTC, rollback at 01:30 UTC if no regression). I have the ACL change prepared and Karthik will execute and monitor.
- Vanessa will coordinate with ClearHarbor to enable MSS-clamp=1380 for the path; if they cannot, we will coordinate a short maintenance to reduce MSS or rate-limit bursts.
- Provide Brightline a temporary credit for the outage window (suggested: one week of usage credits for impacted routes) and a postmortem within 72 hours.

Mike — are you OK with the 1:1 SNAT plan and the temporary credit proposal? ClearHarbor — can you confirm time to enable MSS-clamp?

If approved I'll kick off the change and loop in ops for real-time monitoring.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Support Escalations, Redwood Inference
